name: Brazil
summary: Brazil offers residence for a R$ 1 million property purchase (R$ 700,000 in the North and Northeast; four years, then indefinite) or R$ 500,000 (R$ 150,000 in priority sectors) into a Brazilian company. Remote workers can use a one-year digital nomad visa (USD 1,500 a month or USD 18,000 in the bank). All passports use the same routes; nationals of Portuguese-speaking countries naturalise faster.
naturalisation: Four years of residence (Lei 13.445/2017, art. 65), Portuguese communication and a clean record; one year for nationals of Portuguese-speaking countries under the Constitution; extraordinary naturalisation after 15 years.
dual_citizenship_note: Brazil does not require a naturalising foreigner to renounce (general position; not source-checked in this session).

routes.name: Residence by real estate investment (RN CNIg 36/2018)
routes.summary: Four-year residence for buying at least R$ 1,000,000 of urban property (R$ 700,000 in the North and Northeast), convertible to indefinite residence.
routes.requirements: Minimum R$ 1,000,000, reducible by up to 30% for properties in the North and Northeast; several properties can be added; each co-owner must reach the minimum; financing above the minimum is allowed; funds must come from abroad. Initial authorisation 4 years, then indefinite term on showing the investment is maintained. A law-firm page (25 July 2026) cites RN 36/2018 and no successor; the Ministry of Justice and Labour norms were not read.
routes.physical_presence: At least 14 days (consecutive or split) in every two-year period

Residencia por investimento no Brasil: valores em 2026

routes.investment_options: R$ 700,000 minimum in the North and Northeast regions.
routes.tax_note: Temporary residents without local employment become tax resident after 183 days in a 12-month period (PwC); a permanent visa makes tax residence from arrival.

routes.name: Residence by investment in a Brazilian company
routes.summary: Residence for putting at least R$ 500,000 (or R$ 150,000 for innovation or priority sectors) of foreign capital into a Brazilian company with a job or income plan.
routes.requirements: Share capital of at least R$ 500,000 in a Brazilian company, reducible to R$ 150,000 for innovation and technology, priority sectors or less-developed regions; business plan with job or income potential. Citing Portaria MJSP 65/2023, per a law-firm page; the portaria itself and the status of the 'VIPER' branding were not read. Initial authorisation 2 years per the same page.
routes.physical_presence: Not stated in the sources reviewed

sources.title: Residencia por investimento no Brasil: valores em 2026

routes.investment_options: R$ 150,000 for innovation, technology, priority sectors or less-developed regions.

routes.name: Digital nomad visa (VITEM XIV)
routes.summary: A one-year visa, renewable once, for remote workers earning USD 1,500 a month or holding USD 18,000. It does not convert to residence.
routes.requirements: Created by CNIg/MJSP Normative Resolution 45 of 2021 (per secondary sources): foreign-source income of USD 1,500 a month (USD 18,000 a year), or USD 18,000 in a bank balance; health insurance. One year, renewable once for a two-year maximum. Dependants file separately. Staying 183 days in 12 months can make the holder tax resident.
routes.physical_presence: Up to 1 year per grant, renewable once
routes.tax_note: Tax residence after 183 days in any 12 months (one source says 184); worldwide income then taxable.

open_questions: Brazilian immigration norms (RN 36/2018, Portaria MJSP 65/2023, any 'VIPER' scheme) were not read in the Diario Oficial; investor routes rest on law-firm pages. The brief's 'VIPER' term was not found in any source.
Retiree (aposentado) residence: one unverified source mentions a USD 2,000 monthly pension; not recorded.
Government fees (Federal Police GRU, CRNM) amounts not found.
Digital nomad: legal instrument and income wording rest on secondary sources.
Dual citizenship for naturalised foreigners: Brazil's position (no renunciation required) is not source-checked; only Art. 12 para. 4 on Brazilians was found.
